stories.body: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz after, according to US Central Command, observing preparations to launch rockets and deploy sea mines. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the attack killed two people and injured two others, and responded with ballistic missiles aimed at US-operated bases in Jordan; Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles. Iran also said it targeted an air base in the UAE with drones, though the UAE denied that the Al-Minhad base was hit and said it had downed a drone. The exchange was the first known US attack on Iran since late July and renewed tensions around the strategically vital strait, where shipping remains sharply disrupted.
stories.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes for the first time in weeks

stories.body: Nepal has begun burying hundreds of victims of catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border as the death toll in Nepal rose to 903 and more than 4,200 people remained missing. The flooding, triggered by a glacier collapse, has overwhelmed morgues and devastated roads, homes and hydropower projects. Rescue crews, supported by Chinese and Indian experts, are concentrating on roughly a dozen tunnels clogged with mud and rock where more than 900 hydropower workers are believed trapped. Authorities say nearly 21,000 security personnel, alongside civilians and volunteers, are involved in the response, while China has sent rescue workers, equipment and aid.
stories.headline: Nepal begins mass burials as Himalayan flood death toll passes 900

stories.body: Hundreds of workers are believed to be trapped in hydropower tunnels after a glacial collapse unleashed destructive flooding through Tibet and Nepal last week. Rescue teams are trying to clear debris-blocked tunnels while Chinese and Indian specialists assist the operation. The disaster has killed more than 900 people and left nearly 5,000 missing across Nepal and Tibet, with damaged highways and bridges hampering access to affected communities. China has deployed more than 2,100 rescue workers and life-detection equipment, while India has sent tunnel-rescue officers, forensic teams and humanitarian supplies.
stories.headline: Rescuers try to reach hundreds of workers trapped in Nepal hydropower tunnels

stories.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are among leaders meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's 25th-anniversary summit. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and leaders from Pakistan, Central Asia and Belarus are also expected, alongside Turkey's Recep Tayyip Erdogan and UN Secretary-General António Guterres. The two-day meeting is focused on trade, security and a vision of a multipolar world, as members seek to demonstrate cooperation among Global South countries amid wars in the Middle East and Ukraine and strains on the international order.
stories.headline: Xi, Modi and Putin gather for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit

stories.body: At least eight people have died and 18 or 19 remain missing after a passenger ferry carrying 267 people capsized shortly after leaving Kyrenia in northern Cyprus for the Turkish port of Taşucu. Most passengers were rescued after clinging to the overturned vessel, but divers and Turkish rescue teams are searching deep water around the ferry, which has sunk. Officials said the vessel began taking on water after being struck by waves, although some passenger accounts raised other questions about the disaster. The captain and seven crew members have been detained while authorities investigate.
stories.headline: Eight dead and nearly 20 missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus

stories.body: NASA has launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida on a mission to investigate dark energy, dark matter, black holes and planets beyond the solar system. The telescope separated successfully from its SpaceX rocket and is beginning a roughly 100-day journey to an observing point about one million miles from Earth. NASA says Roman's panoramic field of view will be 100 times larger than those of Hubble and the James Webb Space Telescope, allowing it to map billions of galaxies and potentially discover tens of thousands of exoplanets. The observatory is named for NASA's first chief astronomer and has a five-year primary mission.
stories.headline: NASA launches the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope

stories.body: Flash flooding in the Grand Canyon has killed one person and left about 15 others missing or unaccounted for, as further rain and thunderstorms were forecast for the area. Around 50 hikers were airlifted to safety and authorities closed a number of trails. The flooding damaged infrastructure including a footbridge along Bright Angel Creek and destroyed the area's only water pipeline, prompting emergency water restrictions that prevent tourists from staying overnight at park lodges and hotels. The National Park Service is seeking information about hikers and backpackers who may have been in affected areas.
stories.headline: One dead and about 15 missing after flash flooding in the Grand Canyon

stories.body: A federal judge in Manhattan has again rejected President Donald Trump's effort to move his New York hush-money case into federal court and have his conviction dismissed on presidential-immunity grounds. Judge Alvin Hellerstein ruled that Trump's arguments were neither new nor legally sufficient, writing that paying hush money to an adult film actor or covering up an embarrassment is not protected presidential conduct. It is the third time Hellerstein has refused to take control of the state case. Trump's lawyers said they would appeal, while his separate challenge to the 34-count conviction remains pending in New York's state appellate courts.
stories.headline: Appeals court again rejects Trump's bid to erase his hush-money conviction

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain's cabinet is expected to approve a €168 million recovery plan for Ceuta as the city continues to cope with the consequences of a major migrant influx. He said the government aims to expand reception capacity to 6,000 places and has sought emergency support from the EU, Frontex and Europol. Sánchez also said King Felipe VI would visit Ceuta when conditions permit, without setting a date. He strongly defended cooperation with Morocco, saying there was no intelligence indicating Moroccan authorities caused the crisis and arguing that cooperation is essential to prevent it from worsening.
stories.headline: Spain plans emergency aid for Ceuta as Sánchez defends Morocco and says King Felipe will visit

stories.body: Youth and Children Minister Sira Rego has urged Ceuta to authorize the rapid transfer to mainland Spain of 500 especially vulnerable girls among the unaccompanied minors remaining in the city after the recent migration crisis. Rego said the girls could be accommodated in small centres around the country once the first stage of their cases is processed in Ceuta, but the regional authorities must consent because they hold guardianship. She said roughly 1,478 unaccompanied children are formally registered in Ceuta, including about 700 girls, while the broader total may approach 2,000. Rego rejected calls for blanket returns to Morocco, stressing that any reunification must be assessed individually and prioritize each child's welfare.
stories.headline: Spain considers urgent transfer of 500 especially vulnerable girls from Ceuta to the mainland

stories.body: Italy has extended for 15 days its temporary border checks on people arriving from Spain by air or sea, and Spain has responded by extending equivalent checks on arrivals from Italy. Rome introduced the measures in early August after the migration crisis in Ceuta, citing concerns that irregular migrants could travel onward through Europe; the extension runs until mid-September. The controls do not close the border or suspend EU free movement, though travellers may face identity checks and delays. Reporting indicates the first month of checks found few irregularities and no direct link to Ceuta among those intercepted.
stories.headline: Spain and Italy extend border controls amid the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Spain's regulated electricity tariff is set to post its most expensive August in four years, with consumer group FACUA estimating a typical bill at €96.65, up 19.8% from a year earlier. Other estimates place the bill for a representative household at about €84.50, also roughly 20% higher year on year. Higher natural-gas prices, increased air-conditioning demand during heatwaves, the end of earlier tax relief and a reinforced grid operation have all contributed to the rise. The regulated PVPC tariff, used by about eight million households, is particularly exposed to wholesale-market volatility.
stories.headline: Spain's August electricity bill reaches its highest level in four years

stories.body: Catalonia's education minister, Esther Niubó, has replaced the department's secretary-general, Teresa Sambola, and opened three disciplinary proceedings over errors in the administration of the 2026 PISA tests. The results from Catalonia will not be comparable with other editions because schools excluded 23.2% of selected pupils, far above the OECD limit of about 5% needed for a representative sample. Niubó said the internal investigation found a chain of failures and that only five of the 51 participating schools met the recommended exclusion rate. She said the change in the department marked a new phase, while describing the PISA controversy as a trigger for broader operational problems.
stories.headline: Catalonia dismisses its education secretary and opens disciplinary cases over PISA errors

stories.body: The University of Barcelona is investigating a recently detected cyberattack affecting some of its systems and is working with the Catalan Cybersecurity Agency and the Catalan University Services Consortium to assess its scale and any potentially affected information. The university said it activated security protocols quickly, renewed access credentials and introduced containment, monitoring and reinforcement measures. It said services are operating normally and that no impact on university data has been identified so far, although some websites and services may be temporarily interrupted in the coming days. Students and staff have been urged to be alert for phishing messages or calls seeking passwords or personal information.
stories.headline: University of Barcelona investigates cyberattack and strengthens its systems

stories.body: Catalonia's 2026-27 school year begins on 8 September with 1.6 million pupils, slightly fewer than last year, and 1,103 additional teachers. The education department says it has added 500 reception classrooms for newly arrived students, nearly 5,000 vocational-training places, 582 nursery-school places and additional support staff for inclusive education. It also plans to provide school nurses to half of centres this year. A new guide recommends prohibiting artificial-intelligence tools for pupils under 14 and allowing their use by older students only with authorization and safeguards. Teachers' unions say the measures remain insufficient and have called a strike for the first day of classes.
stories.headline: Catalonia prepares for the new school year with more teachers, vocational places and AI restrictions

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra have arrested a 20-year-old man accused of defrauding at least eight people of nearly €13,000 near Sants station and in Barcelona's Eixample district. Police say he approached victims with stories of personal emergencies, such as being robbed, losing documents or needing urgent travel money, then persuaded them to withdraw cash by promising a bank transfer in return. He allegedly showed false payment confirmations or a banking app to make the claim appear credible, but the transfers never arrived. Police say the total may rise and have asked possible additional victims to report the incidents; the suspect also faces an allegation of violent robbery after reportedly intimidating one victim.
stories.headline: Barcelona police arrest a suspect accused of defrauding people near Sants station and the Eixample
